tagline: Granite mountains, lakes and shoreline linked by an island motor road
intro: The Acadia All-American Road runs from Trenton through Bar Harbor and onto the Park Loop Road, linking the mainland approach with Mount Desert Island’s eastern landscape. The Federal Highway Administration lists a 40-mile All-American Road and recommends three hours to drive and see it. Its description emphasizes rocky shores, granite mountains, lakes and spruce-fir forest. The 27-mile Park Loop Road follows a mostly one-way, clockwise course, with a two-way section returning toward Hulls Cove.

Construction of the Park Loop Road stretched from 1921 to 1958, creating access separate from local streets and the non-motorized carriage roads. John D. Rockefeller Jr. guided the motor road’s completion. He had also developed the carriage-road network after automobiles were allowed throughout the island in 1915, seeking routes isolated from motor traffic. The carriage bridges used hand-hewn local granite and were designed to fit the landscape, with places to view the scenery and to see the bridges themselves.

From Trenton, follow Route 3 across Thompson Island and into Bar Harbor before joining the park drive. The clockwise loop passes Sand Beach, Thunder Hole and Otter Cliff before turning toward Jordan Pond. Beyond the pond come Bubble Pond and Eagle Lake; a separate road climbs Cadillac Mountain.

moments.title: Thunder Hole
moments.text: Thunder Hole is a crevasse into which waves crash, on the coastal stretch of the Park Loop Road after Sand Beach. On the clockwise drive, it comes before the Gorham Mountain trailhead, Boulder Beach and the Otter Cliff overlook. This shoreline alternates between rocky headlands and beaches eroded into stones or sand.

moments.title: Jordan Pond
moments.text: Ice formed Jordan Pond, and glacial debris helps contain its southern end alongside an artificial dam. Penobscot Mountain rises to the west, Pemetic to the east, and the Bubbles above the northeastern shore. The pond reaches a maximum depth of 150 feet and supplies drinking water to Seal Harbor. At the southern end, the original Jordan Pond House restaurant dated from the 1870s. It burned in June 1979; private fundraising financed a new building. A walking trail circles the pond, with branches leading to other park features; a carriage trail follows an adjacent ridge.
moments.notice: The Bubbles rise above the pond’s northeastern shoreline.

moments.title: Cadillac Mountain
moments.text: Before the summit road, visitors reached the Green Mountain Hotel by cog railway. The hotel burned in 1895, and the train was sold and moved to New Hampshire’s Mount Washington Cog Railway. Green Mountain became Cadillac Mountain in 1918, taking the name of French explorer Antoine de La Mothe Cadillac. The summit road followed: construction began in 1925 and ended in 1931. A paved road and hiking trails now reach the summit. Along Cadillac Mountain Road, bodies of black diabase rock record later volcanic activity that intruded into the mountain’s granite.

practical: Thunder Hole: In winter, only the section from the entrance station to Otter Cliff Road usually remains open to vehicles. Check park closure alerts. (checked 2026-10-11)
Cadillac Mountain: During the busy season, Cadillac Summit Road requires a vehicle reservation in addition to a park entrance pass. (checked 2026-10-11)
